title: Insurance Services
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: An earthquake comes under —
questions.answer: C

questions.answer: C

questions.q: The insured is expected to disclose all important facts about the property insured. This is the principle of —
questions.answer: D

questions.answer: A

questions.q: Anil insured his shop against fire for ₹19 lakh. Goods worth ₹9 lakh were destroyed and he claimed ₹19 lakh. The insurer will settle the claim under —
questions.answer: C

questions.answer: B

questions.answer: D

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: A Mumbai company shipping textiles to Dubai buys an insurance policy valid only for this particular trip, regardless of the time taken. (a) Identify the type of marine policy. (b) For what kind of insurance is it mostly used?
questions.answer:
(a) Voyage policy.
(b) Cargo insurance.

questions.q: Match the risks: (a) Pure risk (b) Financial risk — (i) arises from borrowing or investment decisions (ii) involves only the possibility of loss or no loss (iii) involves both gain and loss.
questions.answer:
(a) Pure risk — (ii) only loss or no loss.
(b) Financial risk — (i) borrowing or investment decisions.
(Speculative risk involves both gain and loss; personnel risk arises from illness or death of employees.)

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) ________ insurance is not covered under general insurance. (b) The maximum period of a fire insurance policy is ________ year.
questions.answer:
(a) Life
(b) one

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Insurance is a social service. (b) All contracts of insurance are contracts of indemnity.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — life insurance is not a contract of indemnity.

questions.q: A company took a fire policy of ₹7 lakh. Three months later a fire caused a loss of ₹3 lakh. (a) How much will it get? (b) Which principle applies?
questions.answer:
(a) ₹3 lakh — the actual loss.
(b) Principle of indemnity.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The consideration of insurance is known as ________. (b) The principle of utmost good faith is based on ________ between insurer and insured.
questions.answer:
(a) premium
(b) mutual trust and confidence

questions.q: (a) A man insures his wife's life and they later divorce. Is the contract affected? (b) Oranges insured against accident spoil because of delay in unloading. Will the insurer pay?
questions.answer:
(a) No — in life insurance insurable interest must exist only when the policy is taken.
(b) No — the nearest cause (causa proxima) of loss was the delay, not an accident.

questions.q: Mrs. Shalini insured her life with Bajaj Life for ₹20 lakh and LIC for ₹10 lakh and survived to the end of the term. (a) What type of life policy pays on survival? (b) How much will she receive?
questions.answer:
(a) Endowment policy — pays at maturity or on earlier death.
(b) ₹30 lakh — both policies pay in full, as life insurance is not a contract of indemnity.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the principle of subrogation.
questions.answer: After the insurer has paid the claim, it steps into the shoes of the insured and gets all his rights in the damaged property. For example, if goods are partly destroyed by fire and the claim is paid, the insurer can take and sell the salvage. It prevents the insured from making a profit.

questions.q: Distinguish between a whole-life policy and an endowment policy.
questions.answer:
Whole-life: runs for the insured's whole life; premium is paid throughout; the sum is paid to the heirs only after death.
Endowment: runs for a fixed period or up to a certain age; the sum is paid at maturity, or to the heirs if the insured dies earlier.

questions.q: What is insurance? Why is it called a social service?
questions.answer: Insurance is a contract by which the insurer agrees, for a premium, to compensate the insured for a specified loss. It is a social service because it spreads the loss of a few among many, gives security to families and businesses, and its funds are used for national development.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why is insurance considered important? State any three reasons.
questions.answer:
(1) Security — it removes worry by compensating losses from fire, accidents and death.
(2) Helps business — firms can recover losses and continue; policies also serve as security for loans.
(3) Encourages saving and capital formation — premiums are invested in industry and government securities.
(Also: helps trade, provides employment and social security.)

questions.q: Banita, Promil and Veena insured their godown for ₹10 lakh. A fire destroyed goods worth ₹6 lakh, which the insurer paid. They then sold the half-burnt goods for ₹50,000. Who should get this amount? Explain the principle.
questions.answer: The insurance company. By the principle of subrogation, after paying the claim the insurer gets all the rights of the insured in the damaged goods; otherwise the firm would get more than its loss, against the principle of indemnity.

or.q: Aman took a ₹25 lakh fire policy but hid the use of highly explosive chemicals to avoid a higher premium. After a fire the insurer refused the claim. Can Aman claim? Which principle was violated?
or.answer: No, Aman cannot claim. He violated the principle of utmost good faith — he did not disclose a material fact (the explosive chemicals) that affects the risk and the premium, so the contract is void.

questions.q: Ajay's business suffers from changes in fashion and prices and tough competition; Vijay's from dishonesty of employees and customers and from strikes. Name the types of business risk.
questions.answer:
Ajay — economic-cause risks (changes in fashion, prices, competition; speculative risks).
Vijay — human-cause risks (dishonesty of employees and customers, strikes and lockouts).

questions.q: Distinguish between fire insurance and life insurance on any three bases.
questions.answer:
Nature of risk: fire — uncertain; life — certain (death), only time uncertain.
Compensation: fire — actual loss or sum insured, whichever is less (indemnity); life — fixed sum assured.
Period: fire — usually one year; life — long term.
Insurable interest: fire — at taking the policy and at loss; life — only at taking the policy.
Object: fire — protection; life — protection and investment.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Jeevan insured his property with AIG for ₹6 crore and MetLife for ₹4 crore. An earthquake caused damage of ₹3 crore and he claimed ₹3 crore from each insurer. (a) Identify and explain the principle violated. (b) Explain one more principle of insurance.
questions.answer:
(a) Contribution (with indemnity). When the same property is insured with more than one insurer, the insurers share the loss in proportion to their policies, and the insured cannot recover more than his actual loss. Jeevan can get only ₹3 crore in all: AIG pays 6/10 × 3 = ₹1.8 crore and MetLife 4/10 × 3 = ₹1.2 crore.
(b) Utmost good faith — both parties must disclose all material facts honestly; hiding them makes the contract void. (Or indemnity, subrogation, insurable interest, mitigation, causa proxima.)

questions.q: What is insurance? Explain the principles of contribution and mitigation.
questions.answer:
Insurance is a contract in which the insurer, for a premium, promises to compensate the insured for loss from specified risks.
Contribution: if the same subject matter is insured with several insurers, the loss is shared by them in proportion to the sums insured; the insured cannot claim the full loss from each.
Mitigation: when a mishap occurs the insured must take all reasonable steps to reduce the loss, acting as if the property were not insured; he cannot be careless because of insurance.

questions.q: Mohan took a ₹1,00,000 fire policy. Fire caused a loss of ₹30,000, but he claimed the full ₹1,00,000. Name and explain the principle he violated.
questions.answer: Principle of indemnity. Insurance only restores the insured to the position he was in before the loss; he cannot make a profit from it. Compensation is the actual loss or the sum insured, whichever is less, so Mohan gets only ₹30,000.

or.q: What purpose does marine insurance serve? Explain the types of marine policies useful to exporters and importers.
or.answer:
Marine insurance protects ship-owners and traders against perils of the sea — loss of the ship (hull), the goods (cargo) and the freight.
Policies: (1) time policy — covers a fixed period, usually a year; (2) voyage policy — a particular voyage; (3) mixed policy — a voyage within a fixed time; (4) floating policy — one large sum, reduced as each shipment is declared, useful for regular exporters.

questions.q: What is marine insurance? Explain cargo, hull and freight insurance.
questions.answer:
Marine insurance is a contract by which the insurer (underwriter) indemnifies the owner of a ship or cargo against perils of the sea.
Cargo insurance — covers the goods carried against loss by storm, sinking, etc.
Hull insurance — covers the ship itself.
Freight insurance — covers loss of the freight the shipping company would earn if the cargo is lost or damaged.

questions.q: Explain the principles of indemnity, subrogation and insurable interest.
questions.answer:
Indemnity: the insured is compensated only for the actual loss, up to the sum insured; he cannot profit (fire and marine, not life).
Subrogation: after paying the claim the insurer gets the insured's rights in the damaged property.
Insurable interest: the insured must stand to suffer financial loss from the event — in life insurance when taking the policy, in marine at the time of loss, in fire at both times.
